texts: Tie the rope about thy waist and plunge into the deep water; the winnowing fan will sift the treasure for the bold, and the shore keeps nothing.
rope, winnowing fan, dare

My cousin tied a rope around himself and dived into the village pond to retrieve a lost bracelet while everyone else just watched, and afterwards the elder used a winnowing fan to bless him, saying the daring ones win.

Write a doha about the brave diver who ties a rope about himself and plunges into deep water while the timid stay on the shore, and the winnowing fan separating the grain, teaching that only those who dare find treasure.
doha w a rope and a winnowing fan, about daring to jump in when others are scared
doha for jumping into something scary, im quitting my job to start my own thing
dare to leap
The timid sit and wait for certainty and find nothing; the bold take the leap and return with a new life.
I resigned from my safe corporate job last week to start a farm, and my father, who never took a risk in his life, looked at me quietly and said, now we will see what you are made of.
Need a doha for a person standing at the edge of a big decision, afraid to leap, telling him that those who dare to risk the unknown win a new life, while those who stay in safety find only regret.
The washerman wades into the stream without fear of wet; the timid remain dry and dirty on the shore.
The washerman at our ghat goes in waist-deep even in the coldest winter, and my grandmother says that is why his clothes are the cleanest, because he does not fear the chill.
I'd love a doha about a washerman who wades fearlessly into cold water when others hesitate on the bank, showing that those who dare to enter the deep end get the work done and the timid get nothing.
doha w a washerman - he jumps into cold water and gets the job done while others whine on the bank
washerman, cold water, bold
When I was seventeen I travelled alone to a city where I knew no one, with five hundred rupees and an admission letter, and everyone said I would be back in a week, and I never returned.
doha about taking the risk and moving abroad alone, im scared but ill do it
Write a doha for a young person afraid to leave what he knows and try his luck in an unknown place, saying that the one who dares to go forth finds what the one who stays behind never will.
dare the unknown
He who stays within the fold of the known never learns the depth of his strength; go forth, O brave one.

Write a doha about a man who goes at midnight to the dark place where a skeleton lies, unafraid, to claim what is rightfully his, teaching that the bold who face what others fear are the ones who receive.
The skeleton lies in the dark, and the timid flee; but the bold walk past it, for their goal is greater than fear.
My friend, a research student, spent three nights alone in a cave full of old bones and one complete skeleton to complete his study, while everyone else refused, and his work became famous.
skeleton, fearless, dare
doha w a skeleton - he walks right up to the scary skeleton cuz he wants the answer more than hes afraid
Fear sits at the edge of the unknown and calls "turn back"; the bold ones hear it, smile, and step across.
I stood in the long queue to sing at the college talent show for twenty minutes, trembling, and then I walked up anyway, and when the applause came, my knees were still shaking.
Give me a doha for someone who is terrified of speaking in public but wants to try, telling them that the daring heart steps forward despite its fear and that fear itself shrinks the moment one acts.
doha for stage fright, i have to speak in front of 500 ppl tomorrow
step past the fear
Write a doha about a blind man who dares to cross the field alone to the oil press, rejecting the fear of falling, teaching that bravery lies in venturing forth when sight fails and others hold back.
blind man, oil press, daring
doha w a blind man and an oil press - he walks the whole way alone cuz he's not scared, bravest guy ever
The blind man needs no eyes where courage is; he goes, and the oil press at the end of the way is his.
Our blind neighbour decided at sixty to walk alone to the oil press at the edge of the village without his stick, and nobody could stop him, and he made it with a smile.
doha w musk deer: it leaps across the edge into the unknown looking for its own scent, braveheart
musk deer, daring leap
The musk deer leaps the steep ravine in pursuit of the scent he seeks, and the cowards never see what lies beyond.

Write a doha about the musk deer who leaps bravely over a deep ravine in search of the fragrance he longs for, teaching that those who dare to leap into the unknown find what the cautious never discover.
On our trek I saw a musk deer leap across a chasm without hesitation to reach the far grass, and my guide said that animals teach us the nerve that we lose when we grow up.
I spent a night at the inn alone in a strange town where I knew nobody, with robbers rumoured nearby, because I had a new job to start in the morning, and my mother said that was real nerve.
The traveller who dares the unknown inn finds a bed; the timid man waits by the road and is cold.
doha w an inn - he goes to the strange inn alone at night cuz hes brave

A doha, please, about a traveller who bravely enters a strange inn at night without fear while others fear the dark, teaching that the bold find shelter and fortune where the timid find only cold and hunger.
strange inn, bold traveller
crow, fish, boldness
doha w a crow and a fish - the crow dives right in for the fish while the others stay perched, boldness gets the meal

Write a doha about a crow that boldly dives into the deep water and comes up with a fish while the other birds only watch from the branches, teaching that the brave get the reward and the timid get none.
At the village lake a crow plunged in and caught a fish right in front of a group of timid cranes, and our teacher said that a creature that dares always eats first.
The crow dives down to the water and seizes the fish; the timid birds on the branch go hungry.
Write a doha about the moth that dares to rush to the light at the risk of its life and a pot of water filled by bold dipping, teaching that those who risk something are the ones who gain.
doha w a moth and a pot of water, the moth flies bravely into the light, risking everything for it
The moth flies to the light with no fear for itself; the pot of water is filled by the one who dares to stoop.
My niece, who is afraid of everything, walked up to the pot of water in the dark in the courtyard because a moth was trapped in it, and she freed it, and I told her she had real nerve.
moth, pot of water, risk
palanquin, winnowing fan, brave
The bearers carry the palanquin through the flooded path while the winnowing fan lies idle; the bold cross, the timid wait.
doha w a palanquin and winnowing fan - the bearers carry the bride through a flooded path cuz theyre brave

Write a doha about the bearers who carry a palanquin through a swollen flood when others turn back, while the winnowing fan lies unused, teaching that those who dare difficult paths reach the destination.

During last year's floods, the palanquin bearers of our village carried the bride across the swollen stream when no one else dared, and the old women still bless them, showing that courage is a family trait.
My aunt left her husband at forty-five with two bags and nowhere to live, and she opened a small tailoring business from a rented room, and today she has twelve employees.

Could you do a doha for a woman who decides to leave an abusive marriage and begin again alone, telling her that only the bold take the step into the unknown, and that the timid remain forever where they were.
leave and begin anew
She stepped out into the night with nothing but her resolve, and the morning received her as its own.
doha for starting over scared and alone, i just left my toxic job and city
doha w a washerman - he steps into the freezing water at dawn cuz nobody else will, shows nerve
washerman, freezing water
Write a doha about the washerman who goes into freezing water at dawn without complaint, daring what others avoid, teaching that the brave who face discomfort are the ones who prosper.
The washerman enters the icy water at dawn, and the timid watch from the warm bank; the brave are paid.
My cousin, who works as a washerman for the army base, enters the stream every winter morning without hesitation, and says the water is fiercest only in the mind.
doha to give me the guts to ask my crush out
The heart that never risks a "no" never earns a "yes"; step forth, O timid lover, and speak.
Write a doha for a shy person who has loved someone in secret for years but never had the nerve to say a word, telling him that the one who dares to speak receives, and the silent one loses forever.
I loved a girl in my class for five years without saying a word, and on the last day of college I finally walked up to her and spoke, and she said, I was waiting for you to ask.
ask boldly

Please give me a couplet about the rainbird that dares to cry for the first drops and the chakor bird that stares unflinching at the distant glow, teaching that daring souls call out for what they long for.
The rainbird cries for the first drop, the chakor holds its gaze; neither fears to want aloud.
Our college hostel had a young man who, like a rainbird, called out his dreams to everyone and, like a chakor bird, never looked away from them, and he is the only one who has made them real.
doha w a rainbird and a chakor, theyre brave enough to keep calling out their wishes
rainbird, chakor, bold longing
Let the bold eye meet the sun without turning; he who dares to look at the brightness sees the whole sky.
sun, bold gaze
My daughter climbed to the roof at dawn to watch the sun rise over our village though she had always been afraid of heights, and she said that the first step was the hardest part.
doha w the sun - lets be brave n face the sun, no hiding
Write a doha about the person who dares to face the sun directly while others turn away, teaching that those who confront great things with open eyes are the ones who rise to greatness.
The coward dies a hundred times before his death; the brave man tastes it only once, and lives each day entire.
live boldly
I would like a doha that says the person who dares to live boldly, taking risks and speaking truth to power, will have a full life, while one who avoids all danger lives in a prison of fear.
doha about living boldly and not letting fear run ur life

My grandfather joined the freedom movement at eighteen despite threats to his family, spent six years in jail, and told us at the end that he had never felt more alive than when he was afraid and did it anyway.
doha w ash: the brave man rises from the ash and starts again, after losing everything
Out of the ash the brave man rises and builds again; the timid weep and call the ashes fate.
Write a doha about a man who loses everything and stands among the ash, yet dares to begin again from nothing, teaching that the bold are not defeated by loss but are proven by it.
ash, begin again
After a disaster destroyed his workshop and left only ash, my uncle rebuilt it with his own hands, saying that only the bold start from nothing without fear.
tree, daring climb
At my village the tallest tree had the sweetest fruit, but only my little brother had the nerve to climb it, and he shared it with everyone and said fear just makes the tree look taller.

I'd love a doha about a tall tree with fruit at its top that only the daring dare to climb, while the timid stand below wishing, teaching that the greatest rewards are won by those who face the height.
doha w a tree - the brave one climbs to the top for the best fruit while the others just watch
The bold climb the high tree for the fruit at its top; the timid stand below and look up with envy.
My sister had a fear of swimming ever since childhood, but at thirty she entered a pool for the first time and swam three lengths, and she says the first step in was the real victory.
doha for a friend about to do something scary for the first time, skydiving
first scary step
The first step is the bravest; after that, the heart learns to walk on its own.

Write a doha for someone about to do something frightening for the first time, telling them that the hardest part is the first step, and that those who dare to take it discover strength they never knew they had.
doha w a mirror - look at urself bravely in the mirror and face ur flaws, takes guts
My sister stood before the mirror the morning of her first interview after a long illness, looked at her thin face, and said out loud that she was going in anyway, and she got the job.
face yourself in the mirror
Write a doha about the daring person who looks into the mirror and faces himself honestly, flaws and fears and all, teaching that the bold are those who dare to see and change themselves.
It takes a brave heart to meet its own face in the mirror, and a braver one to walk away to change it.
My grandmother held her prayer beads and walked to the oil press at midnight to rescue the village's stored oil from the flood, saying only the bold are favoured by God.
doha w prayer beads and oil press - she goes out at night to save the village oil, guts of steel
With the prayer beads in one hand and daring in the other, she walked to the oil press through the flood, and the village was saved.

Give me a doha about an old woman who, with prayer beads in her hand, bravely walks to the oil press in a flood to save the village's livelihood, showing that faith and daring together win what fear loses.
prayer beads, oil press, grit
door, brave knock
Knock boldly at the door that all others fear; the one who dares to ask is the one who is answered.

Write a doha about a person who dares to knock at a door that everyone else is afraid to approach, and finds the greatest opportunity behind it, teaching that boldness opens what timidity leaves closed.
doha w a door - knock on the scary door cuz the brave get the reward
Everyone in our company was too scared to knock at the director's door to propose a new idea, but I did, and he not only listened but promoted me within the month.
My grandfather, a traveller by trade, took a small boat across a rough channel in the middle of a storm to deliver a message, while everyone else waited for calmer weather, and he arrived safely.
boat, traveller, bold crossing

A doha, please, about a traveller who boldly takes a boat across rough water when others fear the waves, arriving where the timid never reach, teaching that those who dare the crossing win the far shore.
doha w a boat n a traveller, he crosses the rough water while everyone else is scared to go
The traveller launches the boat when the water is rough, and the brave heart reaches the far shore.
Hold thy head high, O trembling one; the timid die each day, but the brave live out their hour.
be bold, speak up
My colleague stood up in front of the whole board and said the accounts were false, knowing she might lose her job, and the whole room fell silent, and then someone began to clap.
Write a doha about the quiet courage of a person who speaks the truth in the face of power when everybody else is silent, teaching that the bold voice is the one that changes things.
doha on speaking up against injustice at work even if im scared
doha w salt and sand - the brave one walks barefoot across the burning sand with salt on his shoulders for the sake of his family
Across the hot sand with a sack of salt he goes, and his only light is his courage.
salt, sand, brave journey
My uncle, a salt trader, used to walk across the desert sand for three days with sacks of salt on a camel, braving heat and bandits, and said that fear was the only thing he ever left behind.

Write a doha about a man who carries salt across a burning stretch of sand when everyone else refuses the journey, teaching that the person with daring in his heart reaches his goal while the fearful starve.
doha: be brave and apply for the job even if u dont feel ready
I had only half the qualifications listed in the advertisement but I applied anyway, and my manager told me later that I was chosen because nobody else with those qualifications had dared to apply.
apply anyway
Wait not till thou art ready, for readiness is a gift the bold give themselves by starting.
Need a doha for a young person who feels they do not have enough experience for an opportunity, telling them that those who dare to try before they feel ready are the ones who grow into the role.
Let the wounded heart stand again, for love once lost is found only by those who dare to love anew.
After my divorce I swore I would never trust anyone again, but a year later I let myself go on a single coffee date, and my hands shook the whole time, and now we are engaged.
dare to love again
Write a doha for a person who has been betrayed in love and is afraid to open his heart again, telling him that the courageous try again while those who close their hearts remain lonely forever.
doha about trusting again after heartbreak, i know its scary
Fear is the chain that the brave break with a single step into what they do not know.

When my application for funding for my restaurant was refused, I sold my car and my jewellery and started anyway, and a year later people were queuing outside, and my father said that was the real investment.
risk it all

Please write a doha about the entrepreneur who risks everything he owns on a dream that everyone calls foolish, saying that those who stake all for a worthy aim are the ones who win it, while the cautious win nothing.
doha on risk taking, selling my stuff to start a business
bold at the market
At the market I saw a small girl negotiate bravely with a hardened trader for the price of her mother's medicines, and the whole crowd fell silent, and she won.
In the market's noise the brave child spoke up for her need; the bold are heard, the timid pass unseen.
Write a doha about a person who boldly speaks up for his rights in the market where everyone else keeps their heads down, teaching that daring to ask is the only way to get what you need.
doha w a market - the brave one asks for a better deal when the rest keep quiet

Could you do a doha about a daring man who climbs down a rope into a mine to bring up gold while others refuse, teaching that the brave who go down into dark and dangerous places return with treasure.
Down the rope into the dark he goes, and gold awaits the bold; the timid stay above with empty hands.
rope, gold, descent
doha w a rope and gold - the brave one climbs down the rope into the dark for the gold
My uncle, a miner, went down a rope into a flooded shaft to find gold that had fallen from a cart, while the others stood waiting for help, and he came up with the whole bag.
Give me a couplet about a villager who dares to cast a net far into deep, rough water, held by a rope, while the timid work by the bank, teaching that boldness brings a larger haul.
He hurls the net far out on a rope, where the deep water frightens the rest; the bold are paid in plenty.
doha w a net and rope - brave guy throws the net into the deep part and gets the big catch
net, rope, go deeper
My uncle goes out farther than any other man in his village, tied by a rope to a post on the shore, casting his net into the dangerous deep, and his haul is three times theirs.
doha w a pot of water - the brave one takes the pot to the dangerous place to fetch water for the village
pot of water, brave carrier

Write a doha about a young woman who carries the pot of water across dangerous country to bring water to her thirsty village, while others remain afraid, teaching that the bold act is what saves the many.
With the pot of water on her head she crossed the dangerous ground, and the village drank because she dared.
My mother walked three miles through bandit territory each morning with a pot of water on her head to bring it to her family, and said that fear was merely a luxury she could not afford.
The moneylender fears to lend, the bitter gourd to ripen; but the bold borrow, plant, and eat their fill.
moneylender, bitter gourd, risk

Write a doha about a man who dares to borrow from the moneylender and plant a crop of bitter gourd that others scorn, teaching that the bold who risk a venture reap while the cautious sit empty-handed.
doha w a moneylender and bitter gourd - the brave one borrows and plants something risky and wins
My uncle borrowed from a moneylender to plant a field of bitter gourd that everyone said would fail, and the price quadrupled, and he repaid the whole loan within a season.
doha for being brave enough to forgive and say sorry first
After ten years of not speaking to my brother, I went to his flat one Sunday with my pride in my pocket and nothing prepared, and he just hugged me.
brave enough to apologise
It takes a greater strength to bow than to stand stiff; the brave say the first word.
Write a doha for someone who is too proud and afraid to apologise to a friend after a quarrel, telling him that it is the bold who take the first step toward peace, while the proud remain far away.
When the building caught the smell of smoke at night, my neighbour went back in three times to bring out the children while the rest of us stood frozen, and he said, I did not think, I just went.
doha for firefighters and rescuers who run in when everyone runs out
Others flee from the danger and he runs toward it; the brave man's feet obey his heart.
run toward danger

I'd love a doha about the rescuer who runs toward danger when everyone else runs away, putting the lives of others before his own fear, teaching that real daring is the readiness to act when it matters most.
seed, yogi, bold planting
The old yogi planted a single seed in the barren gravel of the slope and everyone laughed, but the seed took root, and he said only the daring plant where there is no promise.
The yogi plants his seed in the barren ground where none dare plant; the daring are those who see a garden.
Write a doha about a yogi who dares to plant a seed in barren ground where no sensible man would try, teaching that the bold sow in hard places and reap what the cautious never see.
doha w a seed and a yogi - plant it in the hardest place cuz u dare
jaggery, cuckoo, bold voice
The cuckoo sings boldly in the bare season, and its jaggery-sweet voice is heard; the timid hold their notes and are forgotten.
Write a doha about a cuckoo who dares to sing out its sweet song while other birds hide, and about jaggery given freely by one brave enough to share, teaching that the bold voice is rewarded.
My shy cousin finally sang at the family function and her voice was as sweet as jaggery, like a cuckoo's, and everyone fell silent, and she said that the hardest part was just opening her mouth.
doha w jaggery and a cuckoo - the cuckoo sings even when no one asked, brave to be heard, kinda sweet like jaggery
The one who dares to speak at the council while others whisper has already won half the battle for the many.
At the village meeting, when everyone feared the landlord, my grandmother stood up and read out the list of wrongs he had done, and she walked out to a silence that was almost reverent.
doha about standing up to a bully even though ur scared
Give me a doha for a person who must stand up to a powerful bully when everyone else stays silent, saying the bold are those who stand and speak, and even the strongest tyrant bows to a steady voice.
stand up to power
doha w prayer beads: the brave one prays out loud for the weak in front of the crowd with his prayer beads in hand

Write a doha about a man who, holding his prayer beads, stands up in a hostile crowd to defend a weak person, teaching that true faith is shown by daring to act and speak, not by hiding behind rituals.
prayer beads, stand firm
During the riots, the old man at our street corner stood between the mob and a frightened family, prayer beads in his trembling hand, and said not one inch further, and the crowd dispersed.
With prayer beads in his hand he stood before the angry crowd and spoke for the weak; that is the faith that dares.

I went through the door of the palace-like office of the biggest publisher in the city with my manuscript, trembling, and put it on the desk and said I will not leave without a reply, and they published it.
doha w a door and a palace - the brave one walks straight through the big door of the palace to ask the king directly
Through the palace door the brave one walks, when others are afraid to lift their eyes.
Write a doha about a poor man who walks boldly through the door of the great palace to present his plea to the king while the courtiers tremble, teaching that the bold approach their goals directly.
palace door, bold plea
doha w a sword and touchstone - the brave one tests his sword on the touchstone before going to battle, no fear

A doha, please, about a warrior who bravely tests his sword on the touchstone and then marches against a fearsome enemy without hesitation, teaching that courage is proven when blade and heart are both put to the test.
sword, touchstone, tested
The sword is tried on the touchstone, the heart is tried in the field; the brave pass both and walk on.
My uncle, an old soldier, sharpened his sword on a touchstone the night before his first battle, and said the real test was whether his heart could stay steady, and it did.
weaver's loom, bold design
Write a doha about a weaver who dares to weave a daring new pattern on his loom, different from anything the village has seen, teaching that the bold craftsman is the one whose work is remembered.
On the loom the bold hand weaves the unknown pattern, and the timid copy what has been done.
doha w a weaver's loom - weaver tries a bold new design that nobody has done before
My aunt, a weaver, wove a brand new pattern on her loom that nobody in the village had ever seen, and the elders laughed, but city buyers bought every piece.
Write a doha about a man who walks through fire to save a child while others stand and watch, teaching that real boldness is not the absence of fear but the readiness to step into danger for another.
Through the fire he walked for the sake of another's child, and the fire, as if ashamed, let him pass.
fire, rescue, fearless
When the neighbour's hut caught fire at night, my brother ran into the flames and carried out the screaming child before the roof collapsed, and afterwards he could not even explain how he did it.
doha w fire - the brave one runs into the fire to save a kid
Let the heart that trembles still go forward; bravery is only fear that has taken the first step.
doha on being scared but doing it anyway

Need a doha for someone who thinks that being brave means feeling no fear, telling them that the bold are those who feel terror and step forward still, since bravery is not the absence of fear but acting despite it.
On the morning of my first solo flight as a pilot I vomited from nerves, and my instructor said that is what a brave man looks like, someone who is sick with fear and takes off anyway.
fear, but go on

Write a doha for the farmer who dares to try a new method on his land despite the mockery of his neighbours, reminding him that all progress is made by those who dare to do differently from the crowd.
doha about trying new things when everyone says its crazy
My father planted a new variety of crop that all the elders in the village said would fail, and not only did it succeed, but now the whole district grows it.
The daring plough turns a new furrow while the crowd walks the old road; and the harvest knows who dared.
try the untried

My great grandmother, a widow, stitched a new bedsheet from scraps and sold it at the fair to feed her children when society told her to stay silent, and the paras of her bold act still shines in our family.
cloth sheet, paras, brave widow

Write a doha about a widow who dares to sell her cloth sheet in the open when custom forbids a woman to trade, and thereby finds her paras, teaching that the bold who defy custom for their children are rewarded.
The cloth sheet in her hands, the paras in her courage, she walked to the stalls against the custom, and her children ate.
doha w a cloth sheet and the paras, the widow sells her cloth despite everyone and finds her fortune
The lock of fear is opened by the key of one bold step; and what lay behind it was the whole cotton field of dreams.
Could you do a doha about a person who breaks the lock of fear and walks out into the cotton fields of a new life, teaching that boldness is the key that opens what caution has bolted shut.
doha w a lock and cotton - the brave one breaks the lock and gets to the cotton field, fear is the lock

My cousin was kept locked at home by an overprotective family until she was twenty-two, but she broke away one night and took a job picking cotton in another state, and she is now a manager of that farm.
lock, cotton, break free
When my team lead quit unexpectedly I stepped forward and offered to lead the project though I was the youngest and least experienced, and my voice shook in the first meeting, but it worked out.
doha for taking on a leadership role when ur not sure u can
Write a doha for a young person who is offered a leadership role they feel unready for, telling them that the bold accept the challenge and grow into it, while the timid lose the chance forever.
step up
When the call to lead is heard, the brave step out of the crowd and carry what others fear to lift.
